notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 52-year-old male admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.84, creatinine 1.08-1.09, hemoglobin 11.5-13, platelets 209-214, sodium 140-141, wbc 9.2-9.5; vitals dbp 73-77, heart_rate 71-74, map 88-91, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-18, sbp 117-123, spo2 94-95, temp 36.6-36.7
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. COPD. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.1-1.12, hemoglobin 10.2-11.1, platelets 208-214, sodium 140-141, wbc 8.8-9.2; vitals dbp 72-76, heart_rate 70-74, map 87-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 117-124, spo2 94-95, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. COPD. Hypertension. No acute blood loss anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 52-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. COPD. Hypertension. No acute blood loss anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
